co_second_grotto_wall.blurb: Second Grotto Wall is a mid-sized cliff in the Grotto Walls group on Independence Pass, above Aspen. It sits uphill of the lowest wall and takes roughly twenty minutes to reach by a rough scramble, which keeps crowds thin. About seventeen routes are mostly trad, with a handful of sport lines. Grades run from the 5.6 range through the 5.9s and up to a solid cluster of climbs in the 5.12s. The left side suits moderate trad, while the right side holds the longer, steeper sport lines, where double ropes help for the descent. Easy warm-ups are scarce. The wall picks up good sun and has a pleasant high-country setting.

co_upper_mother_s_buttress.blurb: Upper Mother's Buttress is the top section of Mother's Buttress in Unaweep Canyon, southwest of Grand Junction. It holds the longer, better climbs of the buttress, on steep walls with continuous cracks. Of the seventeen routes, nearly all are trad and a single one is sport. Grades start around 5.8 and run to 5.12, with the bulk in the 5.10 and 5.11 range, so it suits climbers comfortable on sustained gear routes. Several climbs are three pitches, including the canyon's best-known multi-pitch line. Routes start in the drainage past Middle Mother's, and the descent down that drainage is by rappel, so take care.

co_coaldale.blurb: Coaldale, also known as Cottonwood Rock, is a small riverside cliff beside the town of Coaldale that is best treated as a side trip rather than a destination. The granite is not always solid, but there are some decent lines. A rockslide over a shelf about two-thirds of the way up splits the wall into an upper and a lower section. Seventeen routes mix trad (the larger share) with some sport, spanning roughly 5.7 to 5.12, with the most common grade in the 5.10 range. Many climbs are unnamed. Expect a quiet day out.

co_lower_tier_the.blurb: The Lower Tier is the bottom shelf of the Bihedral cliff on the north side of Boulder Canyon, west of Boulder. Its eighteen routes split between sport and trad, mostly single pitch with a few longer lines, between about 30 and 120 feet. Grades climb from 5.7 to 5.11, with most in the 5.9 to 5.11 band, so it works as a warm-up spot or as a place for harder single-pitch projects. A small slab holds several shorter routes, and there are a couple of easy gully scrambles. The rock is hard, textured canyon granite, and the north-side setting means good sun in winter but heat in summer.
